name: Config / Hardcode / Secret Placement
checks: No secrets committed to Git (including Git history)
No secrets in logs or debug output
No server secrets exposed to client bundle / frontend
Critical env vars have typed schema validation at startup (fail fast if missing)
Env access centralized in a single config/validation module
Business constants live in code config module, NOT in environment variables
Dynamic operational switches live in DB/config service, NOT hardcoded
Infrastructure config (DB URL, bucket name) has NO default fallback value in code
Each config value has exactly ONE truth location (no drift across env + code + DB)
Client-visible config is explicitly classified as public; server-only config is not pushed to client by convenience
Each environment (dev/staging/prod) has its env values defined — no implicit inheritance or missing environment definitions
Infrastructure config is separated from business truth — DB URLs, bucket names, etc. are not mixed with business rules or domain constants
.gitignore alone is not a substitute for secret management — secrets require proper secret manager/vault, not just .gitignore exclusion
Runtime dynamic config implements short-lived cache with explicit TTL — not unbounded cache that silently becomes stale truth

checks.check: A newly required setting must reach the deployment command or manifest.
Where a fallback is provided for an unavailable config service, is the fallback value itself safe — does losing the value open or close?
Can you say, from the diff, which entry a secret arrived through?
Was runtime-fetched or platform-managed secret retrieval available, or was environment injection genuinely required here?

anti_patterns: Secrets stored in repo constants or committed `.env` files
Business truth stored in environment variables (e.g. `DISCOUNT_PERCENTAGE=10`)
Runtime mutable config treated as code constants
Skipping typed validation of loaded configuration
Same config duplicated across env, code constants, and DB without authority rule
Scattered env access without centralized module
why: Review guidance, not an enforced checker or proof of review completion. Apply each question to this repo’s actual scope and architecture; state when it does not apply. Source names and R-/PL- identifiers are historical attribution, not required files in the adopter. Historical measurements below describe the recorded experiment, not a new measurement.
